note: libphext-cfml (CFML on Lucee via CommandBox 6.3.5, embedded Lucee 5.4.8.2, user-level in ~/telephone-cfml on aletheia-core; hand-written canonical JSON, hash(...,SHA-256), binaryEncode/Decode base64; gpg via Java ProcessBuilder /bin/sh -c). Suite green (80 checks, 0 failures; fixtures 16/16 byte-identical + 16/16 normalize-idempotent); remove is coordinate-preserving. v2 adapter self-test PASS; one-shot verify vs games/smoke-001/stress.phext PASS/30 (3.8 s, EE 583). PERFORMANCE PASS (EE 583, after test-001 died at turn ~1005 on validate timeouts): profile on the current test-001 snapshot (2,265,624 B / 1,005 placements) showed explode 5.41 s x2 (per-byte CFML phokenize walk; snapshot is 1,302,022 break bytes) + ~8 s CommandBox boot per hub call, validate needing two calls. In-port fixes: phokenize scans text runs with a Java regex Matcher and collapses break runs arithmetically (coordApplyBreakRun; Java lastIndexOf + replace-all counting — Lucee member replace() defaults to scope 'one'); scrollSort is now a merge sort (implode 3.19 s -> 0.70 s); src/daemon.cfm keeps a warm Lucee context on the hub serving cache/queue, hub/run-cli.sh falls back to the one-shot box run if the daemon does not answer (no verdicts cached; on-disk init cache re-read per validate; daemon exits on source change); adapter GZ1-frames large requests (3.02 MB -> ~0.60 MB) and flushes deferred init on a background thread that validate joins. Game-scale (snapshot copy, turn derived by scale-test-live.py): init 0.10 s deferred, validate 11.85 s and 20.63 s in two runs (target <=30 s; was 40.50 s), choose 7.41 s, apply 13.64 s, all pass. Differential vs pre-pass code (hub-local, old one-shot vs new daemon): verdicts AND fail details identical on pass + placed-tampered + prior-overwritten + unexpected-scroll + index-mismatch (old 28.0-28.4 s vs new 1.1 s per init+validate pair). Lucee pitfalls: buffers are ISO-8859-1-decoded strings (char position == byte position) converted with Java String.getBytes/init because Lucee charsetEncode does not return a binary; struct literals uppercase keys so JSON-bound structs use bracket assignment; canonJSON tests isNumeric before isBoolean (Lucee isBoolean(0) is true); member replace() scope defaults to 'one'.
